newsitem.title: USA: U.S. home mortgage interest rates fall in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. home mortgage interest rates fall in week.

text.p: Mortgage rates fell this week as the bond market welcomed the election election results, leading to lower market interest rates, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
Thirty-year mortgages averaged 7.67 percent in the week ended Nov. 8, down from 7.78 percent a week ago. The rate was the lowest since the week ended March 8, 1996, when it averaged 7.38 percent.
Fifteen-year loans fell to 7.20 percent, the lowest since 7.19 percent in the week ended March 29. Last week's 15-year rate was 7.30 percent.
Adjustable mortgage rates also inched downward to 5.56 percent, the lowest since 5.55 percent in the March 15 week. Last week the adjustable mortgage averaged 5.60 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.37 percent, the 15-year 6.87 percent, and the adjustable loan 5.64 percent.

"Bond markets reacted favourably to election day results, helping to lower interest rates this week," said Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist. "As a result, we have very affordable interest rates which can be compared with mortgage rates in the early 1970s."

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, down from 1.8 percent last week. They charged 1.7 percent on 15-year mortgages, unchanged from last week, and 1.4 percent on adjustable loans, down from 1.5 percent last week.
Separately, the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said the volume of U.S. mortgage applications rose 8.4 percent in the week ended Nov. 1.
Specifically, the volume of applications to refinance mortgages rose 20.5 percent in the latest survey week, while applications to purchase mortgages rose 4.6 percent.
